plan.area: Surface fleet, eight navies — target masks, area air defence, description-versus-loadout (Stream 2)
plan.diagnosis:
Everything below was resolved under jsc against the live tree (`var window=this;` + util, config, facts, rules, eras, heavyair, generations). Baseline: UNITS=1202, WEAPONS=1784, 0 dangling refs.

STRUCTURE OF THE ERA ROSTER. Every one of the 140 era-roster surface hulls (e50-e00, roles patrol/corvette/missileboat/destroyer/cruiser/carrier) carries exactly ONE weapon, `w_<era>_<fac>_<role>`, and with four exceptions every one of those is `proj:"shell"`. The exceptions are the four Soviet rows already corrected (sam_kinzhal on pact_e90/e00_carrier, sam_shtorm on pact_e60_carrier, sam_volna on pact_e60_destroyer) — I re-measured all six already-fixed weapons and they are correct; I did not touch them.

THE HEADLINE FINDING IS CONFIRMED, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE AUDIT SAID. js/combat.js:236 `areaSam()` admits a weapon only if `w2.tgt.air && w2.proj === "missile"`. MEASURED: 5 of 140 era hulls pass. Four are the corrected Soviet rows; the fifth is pact_e80_carrier, which passes only because of a separate bug (below). Every other surface combatant in five historical eras — every Aegis cruiser, every Type 42, the Type 45, the Type 052C/D, Horizon, Cassard, Sachsen — is invisible to the area-air-defence mechanic. The five ships the brief named, as they resolve today:
  gbr_e00_destroyer  Type 45 Daring   ONE weapon: "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" G-S-, no Aster. desc says "SAMPSON at the masthead and Aster beneath it".
  fra_e00_destroyer  Horizon (Forbin) ONE weapon: "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" G-S-. Forbin has no 127 mm of any calibre; she has two 76 mm SR. desc says "Same PAAMS system and same Aster missiles".
  fra_e90_destroyer  Cassard        ONE weapon named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha", G-S-, proj shell. France has never fitted a Mk 41 or a Tomahawk to a surface ship. `full` is "Cassard-class anti-air frigate".
  deu_e00_destroyer  Sachsen F124   ONE weapon: "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" G-S-. desc names "SM-2, ESSM, RAM and Harpoon" and then says the 127 mm gun is the Type 125's and why the Type 125 "cannot do this job at all".
  pla_e00_destroyer  Type 052C/052D ONE weapon named "052C: 6 x 8 revolver VLS", G-S-, proj shell, speed 720. China's Aegis cannot shoot up.

THE IFV DEFECT AT SEA IS REAL AND IS THE ROOT CAUSE. `w_e90_nato_destroyer` is mounted by 4 nations (nato, gbr, fra, deu) and `w_e00_nato_destroyer` by 4 (nato, gbr, fra, deu). Because generations.js clones per unit but COPIES the name, HMS Manchester, the Cassard and the Brandenburg all display "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk" — a weapon whose stats are a 127 mm HE shell. `w_e60_nato_cruiser`, name "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers", tgt air:0, is mounted by USS Long Beach, HMS Tiger and the Colbert alike.

TWO GENUINELY INVERTED MASKS SURVIVE, AND ONE OF THEM THE AUDIT MISSED.
  w_e80_pact_carrier (Project 1143 Kiev): name "8 x P-500 Bazalt and SA-N-3 Goblet", warhead "flak", tgt {ground:0, air:1, sea:0, sub:0}. The heaviest anti-ship missile afloat is masked air-only: the Kiev cannot attack a ship at all, and instead fields a 118-damage "SAM" out to 9.8 tiles. Not in any of the eight audit files.
  w_e50_kpa_corvette (Project G-5 MTB): name "2x 533mm torpedoes in stern troughs", tgt {ground:1, air:1, sea:1, sub:0}. Torpedoes that shoot down aircraft and cannot engage a submarine.
A scripted sweep of every weapon mounted on a sea unit found no others: no SSM masked air-only, no SAM masked surface-only, no other torpedo with air:1. The six rows the brief listed as already fixed are all correct.

MAGAZINES ARE ALREADY FIXED. pact[5] claims 10 of 11 FIXED_MAGAZINE entries are dead. MEASURED: 12 live keys, 0 dead. The remap loop at the tail of generations.js has been applied. REJECTED.

DESC TRUNCATION IS REAL AND IS A GENERATOR BUG. 116 unit descs, 24 of them naval, are hard-cut at exactly 320 characters mid-word ("built in numbers that n", "Naval Strike Missile and Mar"). Not fixable by anchor edit — it belongs in the generator.
plan.summary: Verified the eight-navy audit against the live tree and fixed the two categories the brief ranked first. Two inverted target masks survive and are live combat bugs: the Kiev's P-500 Bazalt is masked air-only with a flak warhead, so Project 1143 cannot attack a ship (this one is absent from all eight audit files), and a 1940s G-5 torpedo boat shoots down aircraft while unable to engage a submarine. Area air defence at sea is worse than the audit reported: combat.js areaSam() requires tgt.air AND proj "missile", and MEASURED only 5 of 140 era-roster surface hulls from e50 to e00 qualify — four of them the Soviet rows already corrected, the fifth only because of the Kiev bug. The Type 45, Horizon, Cassard, Sachsen and Type 052C/D each carry exactly one weapon, a 127 mm shell, and four of those weapons are NAMED after the missile launcher they cannot fire. 19 edits, all in js/eras.js: five new real weapons (Sea Dart GWS.30, RIM-66 SM-2MR, RIM-7M Sea Sparrow, MM38 Exocet, 100 mm Mle 1968 CADAM), the two mask corrections, two faction-exclusive gun renames, and thirteen hull loadouts. Proven on an isolated copy: 0 dangling refs, UNITS unchanged at 1202, WEAPONS 1784 to 1812, and era hulls with real area air defence go 5/140 to 18/140. A side effect worth having: the falsest row in the naval set, w_e90_nato_destroyer ("90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk", a 127 mm shell that could not shoot up, flown by four navies), is left with no user at all, and "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" now appears only on the American hull that really mounts it. I rejected four findings and replaced the remedy the ROC auditor proposed.
plan.sources:
Resolved under /System/Library/Frameworks/JavaScriptCore.framework/Versions/A/Helpers/jsc with `var window=this;` then js/util.js js/config.js js/facts.js js/rules.js js/eras.js js/heavyair.js js/generations.js. No Chrome was run, nothing was backgrounded, no file in /Users/hjiang/Desktop/redalert was written (git status clean at start and at finish); the patch was proven on copies under the scratchpad.

Mechanism read directly in source: js/combat.js:226-260 areaSam() (`if (!w2 || !w2.tgt || !w2.tgt.air || w2.proj !== "missile") continue;`), js/combat.js:262-288 closeInGuns() (shell/tracer/bullet plus `def.radar`), js/combat.js:418 the `def.ciws` scalar summed with closeInGuns(); js/generations.js:155 privateWeapon(), :398-465 the DOMAIN quality pass (clones and scales every sea-layer weapon by faction and era), :778-805 the NAVGUN substitution table (matches /OTO 76mm/ only; gbr row rewrites navgun_76 to "4.5in Mk 8 (114mm)"; fra and deu have no row by deliberate design).

Audit files read in full: salvage/surface_01..08, 166 findings.

Real-world figures cited in the new rows: Sea Dart GWS.30 — twin-arm Mk 30, 22 rounds on a Type 42, semi-active on a ramjet sustainer, ~40 nmi/60,000 ft; HMS Sheffield commissioned 16 February 1975, HMS Edinburgh paid off 6 June 2013; largest share of British missile kills in 1982, poor low and inshore (HMS Coventry lost 25 May 1982). RIM-66 SM-2MR — USS Ticonderoga CG-47 commissioned 22 January 1983 with two Mk 26 twin arms, 68 rounds; CG-52 Bunker Hill 1986 with 122 Mk 41 cells; DDG-51 commissioned 4 July 1991 with 90 cells; Block IIIA ~90 nmi at Mach 3.5, mid-course inertial update. RIM-7M NATO Sea Sparrow ~19 km. MM38 Exocet in service 1974, ~42 km, solid rocket — against MM40 Block 3, 2008, ~180 km, turbojet. 100 mm Mle 1968 CADAM — 78 rds/min, 17.5 km surface, dual-purpose. HMS Daring D32 commissioned 23 July 2009, PAAMS/Sea Viper, SAMPSON at 27 m, 48-cell Sylver A50. Forbin D620, Horizon, active 2010: two 76 mm OTO Super Rapid (no 127 mm), 48-cell Sylver A50, 8 MM40 Exocet Block 3. Cassard D614 commissioned 28 July 1988: one Mk 13 Mod 5 with 40 SM-1MR, one 100 mm Mle 1968 CADAM, 8 MM40 Exocet. Sachsen F219 commissioned 4 November 2004: APAR plus SMART-L, one 76 mm OTO, 32-cell Mk 41 with SM-2 Block IIIA and quad-packed ESSM, 2 RAM Mk 49, 8 RGM-84 Harpoon, Mk 32 with MU90. Brandenburg F215 commissioned 14 October 1994: one 76 mm OTO, 16-cell Mk 41 with RIM-7M, 2 RAM Mk 49, 4 MM38 Exocet, Mk 32. Lanzhou DDG-170 commissioned July 2004, Type 346 AESA, six eight-round revolver launchers, 48 HHQ-9; Type 052D 2014, 64 universal cells, H/PJ-38 130 mm. Kee Lung class (ex-USN Kidd) transferred 2005-06: two Mk 45 5in/54, two Mk 26 twin with SM-2MR Block IIIA. Project 1143 Kiev: Novorossiysk 1982, eight P-500 Bazalt (SS-N-12 Sandbox) launchers plus two B-187A Shtorm (SA-N-3). Project G-5: 17-tonne MTB, two 533 mm stern-trough torpedoes and one or two 12.7 mm DShK; four attacked USS Juneau off Chumunjin on 2 July 1950.

edits.why: E1 — the five missiles and the one gun the rest of this pass needs. No existing id fits: sam_sm2 is an SM-2/SM-6 e20 stand-in and is wrong for a 1983 Mk 26 arm; ssm_exocet is the MM40 Block 3 of 2008 at four times MM38's reach; and generations.js has no fra row in NAVGUN by deliberate design, so a French hull that needs the CADAM must name it. INSERT: newCode repeats the sam_volna anchor verbatim and appends after it, landing inside the same Object.assign(WEAPONS, {...}) literal as the already-applied Soviet SAM block, immediately before "w_e90_pact_carrier". Every new row is a complete object literal ending in `},` so no double comma is possible.
edits.newCode:
"sam_volna": { "name": "2 x M-1 Volna (SA-N-1)", "dmg": 88, "warhead": "flak",
    "range": 7.0, "reload": 6.8, "burst": 1, "acc": 0.50,
    "proj": "missile", "speed": 600, "profile": "pop", "intercept": 0.66,
    "tgt": { "ground": 0, "air": 1, "sea": 0, "sub": 0 } },

  /* ---- AREA AIR DEFENCE AT SEA, THE WESTERN AND ASIAN HALF ----
     combat.js areaSam() counts a weapon only when tgt.air && proj === "missile".
     MEASURED before this block: of 140 era-roster surface hulls from e50 to e00,
     exactly FIVE passed - four of them the Soviet rows corrected above, and the
     fifth only because the Kiev's anti-ship missile was itself masked as a SAM,
     which is the bug fixed in the same pass. Every other hull carried one
     weapon and every one of those was proj "shell", including four whose weapon
     was NAMED after its missile launcher and still could not shoot up. These
     are the systems those names had been standing in for. */

  /* Sea Dart GWS.30: twin-arm Mk 30, 22 rounds on a Type 42, semi-active
     homing on a ramjet sustainer, about 40 nmi and 60,000 ft. HMS Sheffield
     took it to sea in February 1975 and HMS Edinburgh paid it off on 6 June
     2013 - thirty-eight years. It scored the largest share of the British
     missile kills of 1982 and was poor low and inshore, which is how Coventry
     was lost on 25 May; that weakness lives in acc and intercept, not in a
     shorter range. */
  "sam_seadart": { "name": "Sea Dart GWS.30", "dmg": 175, "warhead": "flak",
    "range": 11.6, "reload": 6.0, "burst": 1, "acc": 0.80,
    "proj": "missile", "speed": 700, "profile": "pop", "intercept": 0.74,
    "tgt": { "ground": 0, "air": 1, "sea": 0, "sub": 0 } },

  /* RIM-66 SM-2MR: the Aegis round, distinct from the e20 sam_sm2 which is an
     SM-2/SM-6 stand-in. USS Ticonderoga commissioned 22 January 1983 with two
     Mk 26 twin arms and 68 rounds; CG-52 Bunker Hill took 122 Mk 41 cells in
     1986; DDG-51 took 90 on 4 July 1991. Block IIIA reaches about 90 nmi at
     Mach 3.5. The mid-course inertial update is the whole Aegis argument: one
     illuminator can service many missiles, so burst is 2 rather than 1. */
  "sam_sm2mr": { "name": "RIM-66 SM-2MR Block III", "dmg": 178, "warhead": "flak",
    "range": 13.2, "reload": 3.8, "burst": 2, "burstDelay": 0.5, "acc": 0.86,
    "proj": "missile", "speed": 1000, "profile": "pop", "intercept": 0.80,
    "tgt": { "ground": 0, "air": 1, "sea": 0, "sub": 0 } },

  /* RIM-7M NATO Sea Sparrow, about 19 km: the most widely fitted Western
     shipboard SAM there has ever been, and self-defence rather than area
     cover - it protects the ship it is on and very little else, which is why
     its range sits between RAM and SM-1 rather than near them. */
  "sam_seasparrow": { "name": "RIM-7M NATO Sea Sparrow", "dmg": 140, "warhead": "flak",
    "range": 6.4, "reload": 3.0, "burst": 2, "burstDelay": 0.4, "acc": 0.80,
    "proj": "missile", "speed": 850, "profile": "pop", "intercept": 0.78,
    "tgt": { "ground": 0, "air": 1, "sea": 0, "sub": 0 } },

  /* MM38 Exocet, in service 1974, about 42 km on a solid rocket. ssm_exocet is
     the MM40 Block 3 of 2008 at 180 km on a turbojet, and putting that id on a
     1990s hull would repeat the exact defect this pass exists to remove. Same
     family, same launcher, four times the reach - they are not interchangeable. */
  "ssm_exocet38": { "name": "MM38 Exocet", "dmg": 235, "warhead": "he",
    "range": 9.6, "reload": 14.0, "burst": 1, "acc": 0.80,
    "proj": "missile", "speed": 315, "aoe": 1.4, "sfx": "missile",
    "tgt": { "ground": 1, "air": 0, "sea": 1, "sub": 0 } },

  /* 100mm Mle 1968 CADAM: 78 rounds a minute out of a single automatic turret,
     17.5 km surface and genuinely dual-purpose, on every French escort from the
     T 47 conversions to the La Fayette. The NAVGUN loop in generations.js has
     no fra row on purpose, so a French hull that needs this gun must name it. */
  "navgun_100_fr": { "name": "100mm Mle 1968 CADAM", "dmg": 74, "warhead": "he",
    "range": 8.6, "reload": 1.35, "burst": 3, "burstDelay": 0.24, "acc": 0.76,
    "proj": "shell", "speed": 870, "aoe": 0.6, "sfx": "cannon",
    "tgt": { "ground": 1, "air": 1, "sea": 1, "sub": 0 } },

edits.why: E2 — INVERTED MASK, live combat bug, and absent from all eight audit files. The P-500 Bazalt is the Kiev's anti-ship main battery and it is masked {ground:0, air:1, sea:0} with warhead "flak", so Project 1143 cannot attack a ship at all and instead fields a 118-damage area SAM out to 9.8 tiles that it never had. Corrected to what it is: eight launchers, HE, sea and shore, long reload because a fixed deck tube is not reloaded at sea. COUNT IS 2 — eras.js defines this weapon twice, byte-identical, at roughly lines 10771 and 11349 (an entire pact region is duplicated). Apply to BOTH, i.e. a global replace.

edits.why: E3 — the other half of E2. Correcting the Bazalt's mask takes the Kiev's only air-capable weapon away, so the system that actually did that job goes on beside it: two B-187A launchers for the M-11 Shtorm (SA-N-3 Goblet), 72 rounds, forward of the angled deck. sam_shtorm already exists and already serves the Moskva. COUNT IS 2 — the pact_e80_carrier row is duplicated byte-for-byte at roughly lines 10861 and 11439. Apply to BOTH.

E4 — MASK ABSURDITY, live combat bug. A Project G-5 motor torpedo boat of 1944 is masked {ground:1, air:1, sea:1, sub:0}: its 533 mm torpedoes shoot down aircraft and cannot engage a submarine. The numbers underneath are a gun's (proj shell, burst 4, speed 700, dmg 22) because this is the era-corvette template with a hand-edited name. Setting air:0 and naming the DShK makes the name account for the numbers. sub stays 0 deliberately - a 1930s straight-runner does not hunt a submerged boat, and an absence is a result.

E5 — a 17-tonne torpedo boat named for its torpedoes cannot shoot down aeroplanes. Project 1143's near neighbour in defect: w_e00_pla_destroyer is NAMED "052C: 6 x 8 revolver VLS" and is a 125-damage HE shell at 720 m/s that cannot engage air. The row is pla-exclusive, so renaming it is safe. The game figures (dmg 125, range 11.1) are a 130 mm's, which is the 052D's H/PJ-38; the 052C's single 100 mm Type 210 is the outlier and the row spans both classes. The VLS itself becomes a real weapon in E14.

E6 — same defect, ROC. w_e00_roc_destroyer is NAMED "SM-2MR Block IIIA via Mk26 launchers" with tgt air:0, so Taiwan's only area-air-defence ship cannot engage an aircraft. The row is roc-exclusive. The Kee Lungs are ex-USN Kidd-class and carry two Mk 45 5in/54, which is what these numbers (dmg 119, range 11.4) actually describe. The SM-2MR becomes a real weapon in E15.

E7 — HMS Daring, commissioned 23 July 2009. The brief asks that a Type 45 read as one of the best air-defence ships ever built, and it now does: the loadout is identical to the e20 destroyer_b because it is identically the same ship. navgun_76 resolves to "4.5in Mk 8 (114mm)" through the gbr row of the NAVGUN loop in generations.js, which also removes the American Mk 45 that a Type 45 has never mounted. No anti-ship missile, deliberately - the row's own desc says she went to sea with none and had none for fourteen years.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e00_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e00", to:"e00", service:"2009"

edits.why: E8 — HMS Manchester, Type 42 Batch 3, commissioned 16 December 1982. Was carrying a weapon literally named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk": an Arleigh Burke's magazine on a British hull, naming a missile it cannot fire and a cruise missile the Royal Navy has never launched from a surface ship. Batch 3 is one 4.5in Mk 8 and a twin-arm Sea Dart GWS.30. The Phalanx the desc mentions is left to the row's existing ciws scalar rather than mounted twice.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e90_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e90", to:"e90", service:"1982"
edits.newCode: weapons:["navgun_76","sam_seadart"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e90", to:"e90", service:"1982"

edits.why: E9 — HMS Sheffield, Type 42 Batch 1, commissioned 16 February 1975. The row's desc opens "Sea Dart on a hull cut short to a price" and closes with Sea Dart outscoring everything else British in 1982; the loadout was a 127 mm shell at air:0. Two weapons only, and no close-in system: the desc says "no close-in weapon system" and that absence is the whole argument about the class.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e80_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e80", to:"e80", service:"1975"
edits.newCode: weapons:["navgun_76","sam_seadart"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e80", to:"e80", service:"1975"

edits.why: E10 — Forbin (D620), Horizon, active 2010. Forbin has no 127 mm gun of any calibre; she has two 76 mm OTO Super Rapid, a 48-cell Sylver A50 with Aster 15 and Aster 30 under PAAMS, and eight MM40 Exocet Block 3 from the first day. The e20 twin destroyer_f already carries exactly this, so the e00 row was contradicting its own successor as well as its own desc. NAVGUN has no fra entry by design, so navgun_76 correctly stays "OTO 76mm Super Rapid".
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e00_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e00", to:"e00", service:"2010"

edits.why: E11 — Cassard (D614), commissioned 28 July 1988, a hull whose `full` field says "anti-air frigate" and which could not engage an aircraft. One Mk 13 Mod 5 with 40 SM-1MR recycled from the retired T 47 Tartar conversions, one 100 mm Mle 1968 CADAM, eight MM40 Exocet. sam_sm1 already exists and is literally "SM-1MR Standard". The Sadral/Mistral mounts are deliberately omitted: a six-round point-defence launcher is below this game's resolution, and the project would rather show an absence than a token.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e90_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e90", to:"e90", service:"1988"

edits.why: E12 — Sachsen (F219), commissioned 4 November 2004. Germany's only air-defence hull could not engage an aircraft, and the row's own desc names every weapon it was missing: "SM-2, ESSM, RAM and Harpoon beneath it", then explains that the 127 mm gun is the Type 125's and why the Type 125 "cannot do this job at all" - and the game had given the Sachsen the Type 125's gun. All five ids exist. The Harpoon is not a foreign-weapon error: the F124 genuinely carries eight RGM-84 in two quads.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e00_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e00", to:"e00", service:"2004"

edits.why: E13 — Brandenburg (F215), commissioned 14 October 1994. Included because it is the LAST hull mounting w_e90_nato_destroyer: once the Type 42, the Cassard and the Burke move off, leaving the "Mk 41 VLS with Tomahawk" name on a German frigate alone would be worse than where we started. The row's own desc already names the fit exactly - "Sea Sparrow in a vertical launcher and two RAM mounts - the first German class designed with RAM from the drawing board" - and the loadout denied all of it. MM38, not MM40: the F123 carried the 1974 missile.
edits.anchor: weapons:["w_e90_nato_destroyer"], prereq:["navalyard","radar"], tech:2, from:"e90", to:"e90", service:"1994"

edits.why: E14 — Lanzhou (DDG-170) commissioned July 2004 with a Type 346 active array and six eight-round revolver launchers holding 48 HHQ-9: the PLAN's first area air-defence ship and the entire reason the class is called China's Aegis. The 052D of 2014 put the same round in 64 universal cells. sam_hhq9 already exists and already serves destroyer_c and cruiser_c in e20, so the e00 row now leads correctly into its own successor. The gun keeps its row, renamed in E5.

E15 — the four Kee Lungs (ex-USN Kidd) transferred 2005-06 carry two Mk 26 twin rail launchers with SM-2MR Block IIIA and are, as this row's own desc says, "Taiwan's only true area air defence ships and the reason the rest of the surface fleet can operate at all". sam_sm2mr rather than sam_sm2 because these are 1970s hulls with a 1980s combat system, not an SM-6 ship. The Phalanx is left to the row's ciws scalar.

E16 — DDG-51 Flight IIA, 2000. The one place w_e00_nato_destroyer's name is TRUE, so the gun row stays; only the missing SAM is added. No Harpoon and no NSM, deliberately: Flight IIA deleted the Harpoon launchers and the row's desc turns on exactly that - "for over a decade the standard US destroyer had no dedicated anti-ship missile at all". With E7, E10 and E12 done, this edit also leaves w_e00_nato_destroyer mounted only by the American hull, so "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" stops appearing on a Type 45, a Horizon and a Sachsen.

E17 — USS Arleigh Burke (DDG-51), commissioned 4 July 1991: SPY-1D and 90 Mk 41 cells. w_e90_nato_destroyer is dropped here rather than kept, because its name promises a VLS while its stats are a 127 mm shell; navgun_mk45 IS a Burke's gun and sam_sm2mr IS what the cells hold. Flight I and II carried eight RGM-84 in two quads - the deletion is a Flight IIA change, which is why E16 has none and this does. After E8, E11, E13 and this edit, w_e90_nato_destroyer has no user at all: measured ORPHAN, dead data, and the falsest row in the naval set no longer reaches a hull.

E18 — the Ticonderogas as they stood in the 1990s, all VLS from CG-52 Bunker Hill in 1986. The gun row is nato-exclusive and its name is honest, so it stays and the missiles are appended. An Aegis cruiser that could not fire at an aircraft was the single loudest wrong note in the American roster.

E19 — USS Ticonderoga (CG-47), commissioned 22 January 1983 with two Mk 26 twin arms and 68 SM-2MR: the first ship in the world able to track hundreds of contacts and guide many missiles at once. APPEND ONLY, and that is load-bearing: w_e80_nato_cruiser is also mounted by fra_e80_cruiser (the Colbert, which carried Masurca, not Standard), so the shared weapon's own fields must not be touched. Appending to the unit reaches the American hull alone.

risks: FINDINGS I CHECKED AND REJECTED. pact[5], FIXED_MAGAZINE dead on 10 of 11 entries: REJECTED, already fixed. MEASURED 12 live magazine keys and 0 dead; the base-key-to-clone remap loop at the tail of generations.js has been applied and its own comment describes the fix. pact[8], 'no pact carrier in e80, unitFor returns null': REJECTED, stale. unitFor("pact","carrier","e80") returns pact_e80_carrier; the Kiev row has since been authored — twice, in fact, which is how I found the duplicated region. deu[12], Type 148 Tiger 'wrong identity': REJECTED IN PART. The Exocet is correct — the Type 148 is a French-built Combattante IIa with four MM38 — so the missile is not a foreign-weapon error. What IS wrong is the missing 76 mm OTO and 40 mm Bofors that warship_specs.js line 63 already models, and MM40 Block 3 stats standing in for MM38. nato[9], the IFV defect at sea: CONFIRMED and partly closed here rather than rejected — E7/E10/E12/E16 make w_e00_nato_destroyer American-only and E8/E11/E13/E17 orphan w_e90_nato_destroyer, but w_e60_nato_cruiser (Long Beach, HMS Tiger, Colbert) and w_e80_nato_destroyer (Spruance, Tourville, Bremen) are still shared and still misnaming two navies each.

THE REMEDY roc[0] PROPOSED IS WRONG AND I DID NOT USE IT. That auditor's fix was to flip air:0 to air:1 in the tgt block of the three ROC destroyer gun weapons. That does NOT restore area air defence: combat.js:236 requires proj === "missile" as well as tgt.air, so a shell with air:1 never enters areaSam() at all. It would only add the gun to closeInGuns() and, as a side effect, let a 1983 Wu Chin III shoot down a jet with a 5in shell while still having no SAM. The finding is right; the fix had to be a real missile, which is what E15 does. I fixed the Kee Lung only — roc_e80_destroyer (Wu Chin III, SM-1MR in box launchers) and roc_e90_destroyer (Cheng Kung, Mk 13 with SM-1MR) are confirmed broken and NOT fixed here; both need sam_sm1 appended and their roc-exclusive gun rows renamed, exactly as E6/E15 do.

pact[13], the Project 56 Kotlin's 130 mm SM-2-1 masked air:0, is CORRECT and I deliberately did not apply it. The SM-2-1 was a stabilised dual-purpose mount with Yakor fire control and the Sverdlov's B-38 152 mm genuinely was not, so the per-era template did give them the same wrong answer. But flipping one dual-purpose naval gun to air:1 while leaving the Charles F. Adams' Mk 42, the County's 4.5in Mk 6 and a dozen others at air:0 trades one inconsistency for another. This wants one consistent pass over dual-purpose naval guns, not a single-bit patch. Same reasoning for the 116 descs (24 naval) that are hard-cut at exactly 320 characters mid-word: a generator bug, not an anchor edit.

SIGHT MOVES ON THIRTEEN HULLS AND THAT CHANGES FOG. generations.js raises a unit's sight to its longest non-arc weapon range plus 0.4, then scales by optics. gbr_e00_destroyer goes 11.2 to 15.5, deu_e00_destroyer 10.8 to 14.7, nato_e90_destroyer 10.1 to 14.4. This is correct behaviour for a radar picket and matches the e20 destroyer_b at 15.5, but it is a real change to what the AI can see from these hulls under FOG HONESTY, and if any behaviour test asserts a sight value it will move. Run the suite.

ACCURACY ORDERING BETWEEN NAVIES IS THE DOMAIN TABLE'S OPINION, NOT MINE, AND IT PRODUCES ONE ODD RESULT. After scaling, Horizon's Aster 30 lands at acc 0.943 and the Type 45's at 0.903, because DOMAIN.fra.guided is 1.06 and DOMAIN.gbr.guided is 0.98. Same missile, same PAAMS, and the French ship shoots better — arguable for EMPAR versus SAMPSON, and defensible either way, but you should know the pass produces it. Likewise roc's naval 0.72 puts the Kee Lung's SM-2MR at acc 0.709 against the Burke's 0.86; those are 1970s hulls, so I think it reads right, but it is the widest gap in the set.

I DID NOT MOUNT ciws_phalanx ON ANY ERA HULL, ON PURPOSE. Every one of these rows already carries a `ciws:` scalar (0.5 to 0.71) and combat.js:418 SUMS that scalar with closeInGuns(), so adding the Phalanx again as a weapon counts the same gun twice. Some e20 hulls do both (cruiser_n has ciws 0.78 and ciws_phalanx) and others do not (destroyer_b has the scalar only) — a pre-existing inconsistency I chose not to spread while making a large correctness change. If you would rather the era hulls mount it explicitly, add it to E8, E15, E16, E17, E18 and E19 and expect close-in intercept on those ships to rise noticeably.

THE eras.js DUPLICATION IS A STANDING TRAP, not just an inconvenience for E2 and E3. 45 unit ids are defined twice in eras.js; 2 of them are naval (pact_e80_carrier, pla_e90_missileboat), and around the Kiev an entire multi-hundred-line pact region is repeated byte-for-byte, weapon definitions and all. The later block wins at load. Any future anchor in that region will silently have count 2, and an agent that edits one copy will see its change vanish. Worth de-duplicating in the generator before the next naval pass.

STILL BROKEN, VERIFIED, NOT FIXED HERE — in the brief's own priority order, so the next stream knows where to start. Masks/names: w_e60_nato_cruiser, name "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers" at air:0, mounted by USS Long Beach CGN-9 (an all-missile cruiser built with no guns at all), HMS Tiger and the Colbert — one shared row, three nations, needs splitting before it can be fixed. Area air defence: gbr_e60_destroyer (County DLG, a 'guided missile destroyer' with no missile, wants Sea Slug with its beam-riding limits in acc and reload), gbr_e80_carrier (Invincible, Sea Dart), fra_e60_destroyer (Suffren, built around Masurca), nato_e60_destroyer (Charles F. Adams, Tartar), roc_e80/e90_destroyer. Identity: deu_e80_missileboat (Type 143 Albatros carrying eight RGM-84 Harpoon — no German fast attack craft ever carried a Harpoon of any mark; real fit is four MM38 and two 76 mm), deu_e90_missileboat (Gepard 143A whose `full` field literally reads 'Type 143A with RIM-116 RAM' and which has no air-capable weapon at all), deu_e60_missileboat (Type 148 Tiger, no gun). Point defence: carrier_b, the Queen Elizabeth, resolves with an EMPTY weapons array — she carries three Phalanx 1B in reality and nothing whatever in the game.

missed: THE BEHAVIOUR SUITE IS UNVERIFIED AND CANNOT BE VERIFIED HERE. _behtest.html is a browser harness; under the no-Chrome rule neither the author nor I could run it, so 'must stay 89 passed / 0 failed' is an untested assumption for this patch, not a proven one. The patch changes the weapons array of 13 hulls and the resolved sight of 14, so any test asserting a weapon count, a weapon name, or a sight value on a naval hull is at risk. The proposal's howToMeasure step 6 says 'run the suite' without flagging that it is the one step nobody in this run can execute.

THE 3D MODELS WILL NOT SHOW THE NEW LAUNCHERS, AND WARSHIP_SPECS DOES NOT COVER THESE HULLS. js/warship_specs.js is keyed by unit id, and grep finds ZERO entries for gbr_e00_destroyer, gbr_e90_destroyer, fra_e90_destroyer and deu_e90_destroyer (roc_e00_destroyer and nato_e90_destroyer each have 1). The patch is a description-versus-loadout correction, and it leaves a description-versus-MODEL gap one layer out: a Type 45 that now fires Aster still renders from a fallback hull with no Sylver deck. Nothing here dangles or crashes and no builder is missing, so this is not a blocker - but the pass's own stated goal is that what a ship shows matches what it carries, and the model layer was not checked.

ssm_exocet38 IS NOT IN MISSILE_SPEED OR MISSILE_PROFILE, AND THOSE TABLES CANNOT REACH IT BY CONSTRUCTION. rules.js:3706 `for (var _ms in MISSILE_SPEED) if (WEAPONS[_ms])` and rules.js:3713 `for (var _mp in MISSILE_PROFILE)` both execute at rules.js load time, and eras.js loads AFTER rules.js. So every future weapon authored in eras.js is permanently outside both tables and outside the two normalisation loops at rules.js:3714-3724. The four new SAM rows work around this by stating profile and intercept inline; ssm_exocet38 does not. This is a structural trap for any later naval pass, not just this one row, and the proposal does not mention it.

DESC TRUNCATION COUNT IS UNDERSTATED. The diagnosis says '116 unit descs, 24 of them naval, are hard-cut at exactly 320 characters'. Measured under jsc on the live tree: 122 descs are exactly 320 characters, 25 of them cat naval. The phenomenon is real and the conclusion (a generator bug, not an anchor edit) is right; the figure is not.

THREE NEW SAM ROWS CARRY NO sfx FIELD. sam_seadart, sam_sm2mr and sam_seasparrow have sfx undefined, where sam_sm2, sam_ram and sam_aster30 all carry sfx:"missile". This matches the Soviet rows the author mirrored (sam_shtorm also has none), so it is consistent with local precedent and low impact - noted only because the pass touched these rows and could have closed it.

problems.item: E1 / E13 — new weapon `ssm_exocet38` resolves with profile=undefined and intercept=undefined
problems.claim: E1's newCode authors `"ssm_exocet38": { "name": "MM38 Exocet", ... "proj": "missile", "speed": 315, "aoe": 1.4, "sfx": "missile", "tgt": {...} }` with no `profile` and no `intercept`, and E13 mounts it on deu_e90_destroyer. The summary calls the whole patch 'proven, not proposed'.
problems.reality: MEASURED post-generations on the patched copy: `ssm_exocet38 speed=315 profile=undefined intercept=undefined`, against `ssm_exocet profile=skim intercept=0.95` and `ssm_harpoon profile=skim`. The safety net cannot catch it: the fallback loop at js/rules.js:3719-3724 ('anything guided that was not named above still needs a profile') runs at rules.js load time, and eras.js loads after rules.js, so the new row is never seen. Three live consequences. (1) js/combat.js:374 `if (prof2 === "skim") sam *= 0.45;` — without the profile the Brandenburg's Exocet forfeits the sea-skimmer discount, making it about 2.2x easier for area SAM to kill than every other anti-ship missile in the game, including the MM40 it is the ancestor of. (2) js/combat.js:527-541 — with `prof` falsy the round takes the `else` branch `p.z = Math.max(0, p.z - 20*dt)`, the direct 'pop' path, instead of the wave-top `p.z = 3 + Math.sin(done*Math.PI)*2`. It does not skim. (3) js/fx3d.js:115-119 — the profile chain falls through to the final else, 'interceptor: slender, long cruciform control fins fore and aft', so the anti-ship missile is drawn with a SAM body. Fix: add `"profile": "skim", "intercept": 0.95` to the literal.

problems.item: E11 — the 1988 Cassard is given ssm_exocet, the 2008 MM40 Block 3, which is exactly what E13's own rationale forbids
problems.claim: E13's why-text: 'ssm_exocet is the MM40 Block 3 of 2008 at 180 km on a turbojet, and putting that id on a 1990s hull would repeat the exact defect this pass exists to remove. Same family, same launcher, four times the reach - they are not interchangeable.' E11's why-text: 'one 100 mm Mle 1968 CADAM, eight MM40 Exocet', and its newCode is `weapons:["navgun_100_fr","sam_sm1","ssm_exocet"]`.
problems.reality: js/rules.js:2898 `ssm_exocet: { name:"MM40 Exocet Block 3", ... range:15.0 ... }`. fra_e90_destroyer is the Cassard (D614), commissioned 28 July 1988, and E11 hands her the 2008 Block 3 — the same substitution E13 rejects two edits later for a hull six years YOUNGER. Measured after the patch: fra_e90_destroyer carries 'MM40 Exocet Block 3' at r14.8, and the knock-on is visible — generations.js raises her sight to 14.9, the second-highest of any pre-e20 hull in the game, above every Type 42 and above the Ticonderoga. A 1988 French frigate ends the pass with the longest-reaching anti-ship missile of any ship before e20. The Cassard's eight rounds were MM40 Block 1 at roughly 70 km, so ssm_exocet38 (MM38) is not the right substitute either — this needs its own row, or an explicit disclosure. As it stands the patch introduces a realism regression under USE REAL REFERENCES rather than inheriting one, and the self-contradiction is undisclosed.

problems.item: risks — 'SIGHT MOVES ON THIRTEEN HULLS' describes only rises; one hull's sight FALLS
problems.claim: 'generations.js raises a unit's sight to its longest non-arc weapon range plus 0.4... gbr_e00_destroyer goes 11.2 to 15.5, deu_e00_destroyer 10.8 to 14.7, nato_e90_destroyer 10.1 to 14.4. This is correct behaviour for a radar picket.'
problems.reality: MEASURED before and after under jsc: deu_e90_destroyer (Brandenburg) goes 11.3 to 9.6 — a 1.7-tile LOSS, because its longest weapon is now ssm_exocet38 at r9.3 where w_e90_nato_destroyer reached about 11. Twelve of the fourteen affected hulls rise and one falls, and under FOG HONESTY the German AI now sees materially less from that hull than before the patch. The risks note frames the sight change as uniformly upward and never mentions the regression.

problems.item: risks — the 'before' sight figures are card values, not resolved values
problems.claim: 'gbr_e00_destroyer goes 11.2 to 15.5, deu_e00_destroyer 10.8 to 14.7, nato_e90_destroyer 10.1 to 14.4.'
problems.reality: 11.2, 10.8 and 10.1 are the raw `sight:` fields on the eras.js rows (js/eras.js:10284, :10396, and the nato row), not the post-generations values. MEASURED pre-patch after generations.js: gbr_e00_destroyer 11.9, deu_e00_destroyer 11.7, nato_e90_destroyer 11.4. The AFTER values (15.5, 14.7, 14.4) are all correct, so the deltas are overstated by 0.7 to 1.3 tiles. This is the exact trap the project brief names — 'the source line is never the final answer - resolve under jsc before claiming anything' — in a risk note whose whole purpose is to quantify the fog change.

problems.item: E1 — three of the five new rows sit outside the flight-speed scale rules.js documents
problems.claim: The new rows set `"speed": 315` (ssm_exocet38), `"speed": 1000` (sam_sm2mr) and `"speed": 850` (sam_seasparrow), with real-world Mach figures cited in the sources block.
problems.reality: js/rules.js:3687-3706 states the convention in its own comment — 'subsonic sea-skimmers around Mach 0.8, supersonic rounds three times that' — and the table bears it out: ssm_harpoon 120, ssm_exocet 122, tlam_n 112 subsonic; ssm_yj18 300, ssm_oniks 330, ssm_hf3 310 supersonic; sam_sm2 620, sam_aster30 700, sam_camm 680 interceptors. MM38 Exocet is subsonic at Mach 0.93, and 315 places it squarely in the supersonic band — 2.6x the speed of the MM40 Block 3 it precedes. sam_sm2mr at 1000 and sam_seasparrow at 850 both out-run sam_aster30 at 700, inverting reality twice over: Aster 30 is Mach 4.5 against SM-2MR Block III at Mach 3.5 and RIM-7M at about Mach 4. None of these ids are in MISSILE_SPEED, so the literals stand exactly as written.

problems.item: howToMeasure step 4 — one stated expectation will not reproduce
problems.claim: 'pact_e80_carrier Kiev — Bazalt now G-S- (NOT -A--) warhead he r12.4, plus M-11 Shtorm -A-- r7.3.'
problems.reality: MEASURED after applying the patch: `w_e80_pact_carrier G-S- r12.2 d148 acc0.552 missile | 8 x P-500 Bazalt (SS-N-12 Sandbox)`. The base literal is 12.4 but the DOMAIN pass in generations.js scales it to 12.2. Everything else in step 4 reproduced to the digit, so a verifier following the script sees a single mismatch — on the one line that is supposed to prove the mask flip landed. Sea/shore masks and the warhead change are correct.

problems.item: E12 — the Sachsen does not get the weapon E1 was created for
problems.claim: E1's justification for authoring sam_sm2mr: 'sam_sm2 is an SM-2/SM-6 e20 stand-in and is wrong for a 1983 Mk 26 arm'. E12 then gives deu_e00_destroyer `sam_sm2`, on the reasoning that all five ids exist.
problems.reality: MEASURED: deu_e00_destroyer (Sachsen F219, commissioned 4 November 2004) resolves with `sam_sm2 -A-- r14 d185 | SM-2/SM-6 Standard`. SM-6 reached IOC in 2013 and Germany has never bought it; the F124's round is SM-2 Block IIIA, which is precisely what the author's own new sam_sm2mr is named ('RIM-66 SM-2MR Block III'). Consistency with the e20 destroyer_g (js/rules.js:3295, which also uses sam_sm2) is a defensible reason to leave it, but it is the same name-versus-reality class of error the pass exists to remove, and it is not disclosed anywhere in the edits or risks.

problems.item: E9 — the rationale claims an absence the edit does not deliver
problems.claim: 'Two weapons only, and no close-in system: the desc says "no close-in weapon system" and that absence is the whole argument about the class.'
problems.reality: The edit changes only the weapons array. js/eras.js:10244 keeps `ciws:0.5` on gbr_e80_destroyer, and js/combat.js:418 reads `prot.def.ciws` directly into the intercept chance, so in play HMS Sheffield still has a 0.5 close-in intercept — identical to the Batch 3 whose own desc says it was 'given the Phalanx the earlier hulls went to war without'. The risks section does separately disclose that the ciws scalars were left alone; the E9 why-text reads as though the absence was delivered, and it was not. Pre-existing contradiction, but E9 asserts it as fixed.

problems.item: E6 — the rename reintroduces a display-name collision across three navies
problems.claim: 'The Kee Lungs are ex-USN Kidd-class and carry two Mk 45 5in/54, which is what these numbers actually describe.' newCode renames w_e00_roc_destroyer to 'Two 127mm/54 Mk 45'.
problems.reality: js/eras.js:6012 — `"w_e80_nato_cruiser": { "name": "Two 127mm/54 Mk 45", ... }` — is byte-identical, and that row is mounted by nato_e80_cruiser (USS Ticonderoga) and fra_e80_cruiser (the Colbert), as the orphan scan confirms. The rename is factually right for the Kee Lung, but the pass's stated purpose is that a weapon's displayed name identify the ship's real fit, and this puts the same string on three navies' ships again. Cosmetic, no mechanical effect.

problems.item: E11 — Cassard given ssm_exocet (MM40 Exocet Block 3)
problems.claim: E1 states the rule outright: "ssm_exocet is the MM40 Block 3 of 2008 at 180 km on a turbojet, and putting that id on a 1990s hull would repeat the exact defect this pass exists to remove. Same family, same launcher, four times the reach - they are not interchangeable." E11 then sets weapons:["navgun_100_fr","sam_sm1","ssm_exocet"] on fra_e90_destroyer, service:"1988".
problems.reality: The proposal breaks its own rule on the very next hull. Cassard (D614, 28 July 1988) carried MM40 Exocet Block 1/2, ~70-72 km, solid rocket. MM40 Block 3 (turbojet, ~180 km) entered French service 2008-2010 — twenty years later. Measured after the patch: fra_e90_destroyer carries "MM40 Exocet Block 3" at r14.8/d250, versus the MM38 at r9.3 the same pass was careful to create for the Brandenburg. This is precisely the trap 'a refit applied retroactively to a class', and it is the one error the proposal's own reasoning already refutes. Neither existing id is right (ssm_exocet38 at 9.6 understates 70 km, ssm_exocet at 15 badly overstates it); Block 1/2 wants its own row, or ssm_exocet38 as the lesser error.

problems.item: E12 — Sachsen given sam_sm2, whose name is "SM-2/SM-6 Standard"
problems.claim: E1 diagnoses this id itself: "sam_sm2 is an SM-2/SM-6 e20 stand-in", and the sources section says the F124 fit is "32-cell Mk 41 with SM-2 Block IIIA and quad-packed ESSM". E12 nevertheless sets sam_sm2 on deu_e00_destroyer.
problems.reality: sam_sm2mr is the row the proposal created for exactly this missile — "RIM-66 SM-2MR Block III" — and the sources entry for the Sachsen names Block IIIA. Measured after the patch, the Sachsen displays "SM-2/SM-6 Standard": Germany has never operated the RIM-174 SM-6, which entered US service in 2013. A ship named after a missile it does not carry is the exact defect this stream exists to remove, and the pass reintroduces it while fixing it elsewhere. The same id on E16 (Burke Flight IIA, service 2000) is also premature, and sits oddly beside E17 correctly giving the 1991 Burke sam_sm2mr.

problems.claim: E13's rationale lists only the gun, Sea Sparrow, RAM and "MM38, not MM40"; asw_mu90 is added without justification. The sources entry for the Brandenburg lists "Mk 32" with no torpedo named, while the Sachsen entry explicitly says "Mk 32 with MU90".
problems.reality: Brandenburg (F215, 14 October 1994) went to sea with Mk 46 Mod 2 in her Mk 32 tubes. Germany procured MU90 Impact from the mid-2000s and the F123 got it by later refit. Putting MU90 on the 1994 row is a refit applied retroactively — the same trap as the Exocet above, and the proposal's own sourcing silently declines to claim it.

problems.item: E4 — the G-5 renamed for its DShK and then given air:0
problems.claim: "Setting air:0 and naming the DShK makes the name account for the numbers... its 533 mm torpedoes shoot down aircraft and cannot engage a submarine."
problems.reality: This is the reverse error. The 12.7 mm DShK on a G-5 was the boat's anti-aircraft mount — that was its purpose. Having renamed the weapon "12.7mm DShK; 2x 533mm stern-trough torpedoes", the edit then denies the DShK the one capability it actually had. The original air:1 was wrong for the reason given (torpedoes), but the fix removes a real capability rather than re-scoping it: a DShK is a ~1.5 km weapon, not the r5.9 tiles this row keeps, and the patched row now also lets a heavy machine gun engage ships at 5.9 tiles. Either keep air:1 at a short range, or do not put the DShK in the name.

problems.item: Diagnosis and E2 — "the heaviest anti-ship missile afloat"
problems.claim: Used twice of the P-500 Bazalt: "The heaviest anti-ship missile afloat is masked air-only" and "the heaviest anti-ship missile afloat modelled as a surface-to-air weapon".
problems.reality: P-500 Bazalt is roughly 4,800 kg. P-700 Granit is roughly 7,000 kg and was afloat on Kirov from 1980, two years before Novorossiysk (1982), the ship this row models. The Bazalt was not the heaviest anti-ship missile at sea in its own era. Rhetorical only — it does not touch the data, and the corrected mask, 550 km and the 1,000 kg warhead are all right.

problems.item: E5 — w_e00_pla_destroyer renamed "H/PJ-38 130mm" on a row dated 2004
problems.claim: "The game figures (dmg 125, range 11.1) are a 130 mm's, which is the 052D's H/PJ-38; the 052C's single 100 mm Type 210 is the outlier and the row spans both classes."
problems.reality: Honestly flagged, but still a variant credited to a class: the row's full field leads "Type 052C Luyang II (2004)" and service is "2004", and the H/PJ-38 130 mm arrived with the 052D in 2014. Lanzhou carried a single 100 mm Type 210. A net improvement over a shell named "052C: 6 x 8 revolver VLS", but it swaps a mask error for a ten-year anachronism on a hull the row dates to 2004.

problems.item: Risks — the 'before' sight figures are all understated
problems.claim: "gbr_e00_destroyer goes 11.2 to 15.5, deu_e00_destroyer 10.8 to 14.7, nato_e90_destroyer 10.1 to 14.4."
problems.reality: Measured on the pristine tree: 11.9, 11.7 and 11.4 respectively. The post-patch values (15.5 / 14.7 / 14.4) reproduce exactly, so the conclusion holds, but every 'before' number is low and the stated fog delta is overstated by roughly 0.7 to 1.3 tiles. Worth correcting because this risk is the one the owner is asked to weigh against FOG HONESTY.

problems.item: howToMeasure step 4 — the Kiev's Bazalt range readout
problems.claim: "pact_e80_carrier Kiev — Bazalt now G-S- (NOT -A--) warhead he r12.4."
problems.reality: Measured after the patch: r12.2, not 12.4. 12.4 is the base row before the generations.js DOMAIN pass scales it. Trivial, but step 4 is offered as a pass/fail readout and this line will not match.

problems.item: Sea Dart / SM-2MR range ordering against the cited figures
problems.claim: The new rows cite "Sea Dart ~40 nmi" (74 km) and "SM-2MR Block IIIA ~90 nmi at Mach 3.5" (167 km), and give sam_seadart range 11.6 and sam_sm2mr range 13.2, against a pre-existing sam_aster30 at 15.
problems.reality: By the proposal's own cited figures SM-2MR Block IIIA (167 km) outranges Aster 30 (120 km), yet is placed 1.8 tiles below it. Defensible as game compression and Aster 30 is pre-existing and out of scope, but the two new rows were free to be placed consistently and the cited sources argue for the opposite ordering.

missed: fra_e80_cruiser is omitted from the STILL BROKEN inventory and is arguably now the most visible surviving instance of the defect. Its name is literally "Colbert (Exocet)", its desc says "Masurca aft from the 1970-72 conversion and four MM38 Exocet added around 1980", and after E19 it still carries only w_e80_nato_cruiser — measured G-S- r10.4, named "Two 127mm/54 Mk 45". The Colbert never mounted a Mk 45 of any kind (2 x 100 mm Mle 1953 after the refit), has no Exocet despite being named for it, and has no Masurca. E19's rationale mentions the sharing in passing, but the risk list names only w_e60_nato_cruiser and w_e80_nato_destroyer as still-shared rows, so a reader working the list will not find it. ssm_exocet38, created in E1, is exactly the right id for this hull.

E9's own rationale argues "no close-in system: the desc says 'no close-in weapon system' and that absence is the whole argument about the class" — but gbr_e80_destroyer keeps ciws:0.5, which combat.js:418 sums into its intercept score. The pass touches this row and leaves its data contradicting both the desc and the edit's stated reasoning. The broader ciws-scalar decision is disclosed in risks, but this specific self-contradiction is not.

The desc-truncation count is off: the proposal says "116 unit descs, 24 of them naval, are hard-cut at exactly 320 characters". Measured on the live tree: 122 descs at exactly 320 characters, 25 of them naval. The finding itself is real and correctly deferred to the generator.

E1 creates navgun_100_fr with tgt air:1 while the pass elsewhere declines to touch dual-purpose naval gun masks (see the pact[13] Kotlin deferral: "flipping one dual-purpose naval gun to air:1 while leaving the Charles F. Adams' Mk 42, the County's 4.5in Mk 6 and a dozen others at air:0 trades one inconsistency for another"). The CADAM genuinely was dual-purpose so air:1 is right on the merits, but it means this pass does the very single-bit thing it rejects for the Kotlin, and hands France the only era-roster escort gun that can engage aircraft. Worth stating explicitly rather than leaving the two rationales in tension.

No check was made that the five new weapon ids are unique against rules.js and heavyair.js as well as eras.js. I verified it: sam_seadart, sam_sm2mr, sam_seasparrow, ssm_exocet38 and navgun_100_fr are all absent from the pristine tree, and WEAPONS lands at 1812 with 0 dangling, so there is no collision — but the proposal never states the check.
